General rule of thumb for wireless communication: lower frequencies equal longer range and better penetration, but lower bandwidth. Higher frequencies equal less range and penetration but higher bandwidth. That's why 2.4GHz gets better range than 5GHz but 5GHz has more bandwidth than 2.4GHz. Thus, going all the way down to 900MHz means much better range (they say 1km), but drops the bandwidth down so the speed is only 100kbps.

Saw that coming before opening the comments. It has it's use and place to have a higher range at the cost of speed but this won't be something useful for at home usage. Sucks that Engadget didn't mention this

100Kbs max at the smallest channel size in a single antenna mode (SISO). This "HAY-LOW" stuff is an extension of the standard to allow for even smaller channels. At larger channels its capable of some really decent throughput like upwards of ~40Mbs. And has the possibility of up to 4X4 channels (MIMO). Of course larger channel size means more interference and shorter range. Check out the IEEE database if your interested.
